_comment: The Empire. Seven polities, three reigns. Cap the polity list at nine forever: learnability is the whole game, and each one must carry exactly one mechanical habit a player can hold in their head.
day_heading: The eleventh day of October, in the seventh year of Kunrad IV. Third desk, second floor. Four matters heard.
_day_note: One candle is one working day. Listening is free until the notary first handles a matter. From that physical engagement onward it burns through thought and speech until judgment. It does not burn between callers or while the ledger is open.
day_burnt_out: The candle went before the queue did. The doorkeeper turned the rest of them out into the passage and told them to come back on Thursday.

desk_note.title: Memorandum
desk_note._geometry_note:
Left edge must clear the right edge of the widest charter (430 wide, laid at x=-45, so ending at x=175); this sheet spans 198..598. It is built AFTER the books in Desk._build_fixtures so it draws on top of them; before that change the Almanac covered 255 units of it and everything below 'It is not a man alive' was unreadable at dawn.

NINE SENTENCES. Thirteen more were here and they were the whole over-teaching problem: eleven teachable things before the second knock. Four moved onto leaves delivered by day_01's after_case / after_investigation channels, and four were retired to the books that already carry them permanently — a delivered slip is destroyed at the next dawn (lay_out_day_documents frees every day_paper), so deferring a sentence a book already holds would make it LESS available, not more.

What survives is only what a cold player is harmed by not knowing: the glass bites at the foot of a charter and nowhere else (lens.gd:175 picks by detail_centre within 98.6 units), a regnal year has to be reduced, the tablet and stylus exist at all (both are near-invisible in the dark), the Kalendar is the green one, how to make wax at all — without which the player is STUCK rather than merely wrong — that the wax is final, and the candle rule. The candle rule cannot be deferred by any channel: after_investigation requires stage WORKING, by which time the clock is already running.
desk_note.petitioner_style: left beneath the Register, in R.V.'s hand
desk_note.claim_summary: Read the wax with the glass, and the small hand at the foot of a charter with it. Read the years against the Almanac.
desk_note.received_note:
There is a tablet in the rack and a stylus by your left hand. The green book in the rack is the Kalendar.

Melt the resin cake in the brass spoon, lift it clear of the flame, and pour. One ring. When the wax gives, judgment is made. There is no second impression.
desk_note.doorkeeper_note: Once you disturb a matter, the candle waits on neither thought nor tongue. — R.V.

practice_documents.title: Before the door opens
practice_documents.petitioner_style: discarded office leaf; no party is bound
practice_documents.claim_summary: Read the memorandum. Hold the leaf up to the flame and see what the knife took out. Then melt, pour, choose a ring, and hold until the wax gives. The first knock waits.
practice_documents.doorkeeper_note: Afterward, hold the glass over your impression until the door opens. Four in the passage, and two have brought their own chairs.

practice_documents.title: Discarded Practice Leaf
practice_documents.body_text:
THIS LEAF TRANSFERS NOTHING.

Strike one complete office device below. Feel the resistance before the wax yields. Once it gives, the judgment cannot be changed; continue to hold for a clean device, then lift without dragging.

Somebody has been at the year on this leaf with a knife. Pick the sheet up and hold it in front of the flame before you seal it, so that you know what that looks like the first time it matters.

erasures._note: Over the rubric date line, measured from a capture. The practice leaf teaches the fourth verb because it transfers nothing and cannot be got wrong.
erasures.original_value: in the fourth year of Kunrad IV

_reigns_note: election_year is when he was chosen King of the Romans, in his predecessor's lifetime. accession_year is when the predecessor died. coronation_year is the imperial crown at Rome. The gaps between these three are what make a regnal date ambiguous, and they are the engine of every date puzzle in the game.

reigns.name: Otbert
reigns.epithet: who held the crown twenty-six years and left it contested
reigns.note: Two years between his election and his accession. The Church counts them; the Chancery does not.

reigns.name: Aldric
reigns.epithet: chosen young, crowned late, dead at Marchfeld
reigns.note: Elected King of the Romans three years before Otbert died. His eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth years exist by one reckoning and not by another.

reigns.name: Kunrad
reigns.note: Elected in Aldric's lifetime, as is now the custom. Crowned four years after.

polities.name: The Crown of Aachen-Verd
polities.succession: Elective. Seven electors, and never yet a quiet one.
polities.note: The Chancery's own authority. Its notaries count an emperor's years from the day the last one died, and regard every other reckoning as a courtesy.

polities.name: The Margraviate of Thurn
polities.succession: Male primogeniture. The eldest son takes all of it.
polities.note: A Thurn matrix is defaced before witnesses on the day its holder dies, so that no man may seal in a dead man's name. They are proud of this.

polities.name: The Free City of Marchfeld
polities.succession: An elected council. The Burgomaster serves three years and then goes back to his trade.
polities.note: The city's seal belongs to the office and not the man. It has outlasted eleven Burgomasters and will outlast the twelfth. A Marchfeld die is almost never dead.

polities.name: The Prince-Bishopric of Saint Wend
polities.succession: By election of the cathedral chapter. No heirs, by definition.
polities.note: Dates its instruments from the day an emperor was chosen, not the day he acceded. This is not an error and they will not be corrected.

polities.name: The Duchy of Ostmark
polities.succession: Partible. The land is divided among all sons, and among all their sons after.
polities.note: Ostmark charters cite fractions, and two brothers may hold perfectly valid claims to the same mill. Nothing about this is a forgery. It is simply how they inherit.

polities.name: The County of Hallenstein
polities.succession: Agnatic. No woman inherits, and no claim passes through one.
polities.note: A widow of Hallenstein holds nothing. She may live on her husband's land at the pleasure of his heir, which is not the same as holding it, as the heirs are careful to explain.

polities.name: The Wends of the Nether March
polities.succession: By the agreement of the elders, recorded in nobody's hand.
polities.note: They keep no seals. A grant is witnessed by oath and by named men standing in a field, and holds for as long as those men live and can be found. Wax on a Wendish instrument was put there by somebody who wanted it to look like ours.
